scope: Real account HTTP, controlled replies through the existing worker connection and actual SQL. The production Rust executable ran with external PostgreSQL. The same source's development SQL fixture ran with PGlite and bundled PostgreSQL.
observations: A foreign owner received 404. Stale revisions and unknown destinations returned typed conflicts. Replaying the same operation returned its receipt, and changed inputs under that operation ID conflicted.
The transfer incremented the dispatch fence and retained the canonical encrypted message. It remained draining until a replacement worker connection acknowledged settlement.

After acknowledgment Rust completed the transfer at revision 4. The Node reference stayed draining at revision 3 after repeated positive acknowledgments. The stored JSONB source and schema-shaped source had identical fields in different order. The reference compares them by JSON serialization.

An older Rust test binary returned HTTP 500 on successful admission and lacked the provider-transfer eligibility migration. The rebuilt fixture includes that migration and completed the operation on both local stores.

fullWorkerReconnect.scope: The macOS ARM64 1.1.2881 packaged server and worker executed both HTTP routes and the worker revocation for a previously queued Task on each store. The Task and its encrypted input were seeded. A development SQL executable seeded and inspected the two local databases in separate, stopped-server phases. The external PostgreSQL case used a direct database connection for those checks.

activeDispatchRejection.scope: The existing browser SDK started the Task through the packaged Node worker and bundled Codex on external PostgreSQL. A loopback model provider held the actual response stream after first dispatch. The fixture used read-only SQL to inspect the active receipt and verify that the rejected provider change left the Task, dispatch fence, and inference input unchanged. Releasing the original response completed the Task.

linuxContainers.scope: Production Rust Linux ARM64 and x64 containers connected to isolated external PostgreSQL databases. The unchanged packaged macOS ARM64 worker connected over HTTP and WebSocket. The x64 Linux executable ran under Rosetta, with its mapped ELF inode and artifact hash verified. Queued transfer used seeded encrypted input. The browser SDK, bundled Codex and a loopback model fixture exercised active dispatch, with a read-only database comparison around the rejected request.

linuxLocalStores.scope: Exact production Linux images with the packaged macOS ARM64 worker. The earlier 1.1.2881 images cover bundled PostgreSQL on both architectures and PGlite on ARM64. The rebuilt ARM64 and x64 images include the Task route snapshot repair and passed both cases on all three stores. PGlite queued cases seeded a separate profile through native logical export and restore, then verified final state from a stopped-server export. PGlite active dispatch compared scoped Task rows from two frozen copies, exported each copy with the native binary, and queried the imports read-only in a disposable PostgreSQL instance.

rebuiltWindowsArtifact.scope: Windows 11 x64 under QEMU on macOS ARM64. Exact packaged server and existing worker, isolated persisted profiles, offline fixture SQL for initial Task state, real HTTP, worker reconnection and database restart.

earlierDriverFailures.failure: Bundled test driver attempted to invoke rustc in the Windows guest.
The exit timer included the Windows query that verified the process tree after exit.

currentLinuxArtifactTaskFaults.scope: Actual Linux server images, local macOS browser and packaged worker. Active-dispatch cases hold the fixture model response during the transfer. The deterministic settlement read uses external PostgreSQL and a held table lock. Linux x64 executes through Rosetta in Docker Desktop.

currentWindowsSettlementRead.scope: Windows 11 x64 in local QEMU. Exact packaged server with a disposable external PostgreSQL cluster. The production HTTP GET crosses a deliberately held database lock while the Task revision and transfer phase settle in one transaction.

currentWindowsActiveDispatch.workerTeardown: Windows taskkill observed eight process identities and verified the owned tree was gone.
